facts.claim: Grace Hotel Santorini (Auberge Resorts Collection) is in Imerovigli, Santorini; its Weddings page describes a 'dramatic cliffside location' and 'intimate scale', perched on a clifftop above the Aegean, with ceremonies 363 metres above sea level facing caldera sunsets. Venue type: cliff-top suite hotel.

Grace Hotel's wedding venues as published: 363 Lounge (open-air champagne lounge terrace facing the sunset) seated 40 / standing 60; The Villa (a 400 sq m villa with private pool, gazebo and outdoor fireplace, described as among the largest in the Cyclades) seated 15 / standing 60. Couples may exchange vows on the villa terrace.
Grace Hotel offers a unity ceremony in which the couple combine black and white volcanic sand collected from Santorini beaches.

Grace Hotel: a flat venue fee applies and includes exclusive use of the selected event spaces, furniture, set-up and breakdown and staffing; packages differ for 50 guests or fewer and for over 50 guests. Amount not recorded.
Grace Hotel requires a wedding planner for all weddings, involved for a minimum of 3 months before the wedding; the hotel provides a dedicated event manager for venue details.

Grace Hotel: guests may book individually; room blocks or a resort buyout are quoted by the Sales Manager on request, and the hotel states it does not require a minimum number of rooms to be booked. Total room count not published on the Weddings page.
Grace Hotel: a private lounge with full-length mirror is available to the wedding party from 8am on the wedding day; a DJ or live band may play at the reception.

Canaves Collection (Oia) lists three wedding venues: Panorama Balcony at Canaves Oia Suites (up to 30 guests, caldera view), Veranda at Canaves Sunday (rooftop, up to 40 guests, 180-degree caldera views) and Sunset Terrace at Canaves Epitome (up to 25 guests). Venue type: caldera hotel collection.

Canaves Collection's wedding enquiry form lists ceremony types Religious, Civil, Symbolic and Vow Renewal, and the page says it caters for 'traditional weddings to modern elopements'. A wedding brochure PDF with package options is linked.

Canaves Collection's site navigation lists an 'Exclusives & Buyouts' page under Events & Weddings (page not re-read in this batch; exclusive-use terms not recorded). Properties listed: Canaves Ena, Canaves Oia Suites, Canaves Epitome, Canaves Sunday, plus The Villas.

Katikies Hotels list Santorini properties Katikies Santorini (Pelagos House and Gea House, Oia), Katikies Chromata (Imerovigli) and Katikies Garden (Fira); the Events page names Weddings and 'Hotel Take over' among event types.

Katikies Santorini (Oia): Botrini's Restaurant seated 60 / standing 100, described as ideal for wedding ceremonies, lunches, dinners and standing cocktail receptions; Katikies Lounge Lower Deck seated 50 / standing 100.
Katikies Garden (Fira): St. Joseph Wine Cave seated 36 / standing 50 and Garden Pool Bar seated 36 / standing 100, both described as ideal for wedding ceremonies; Selene Restaurant standing 150.
Katikies Chromata (Imerovigli): Koukoumavlos Restaurant Deck seated 20 / standing 50 and Chromata Pool Bar area seated 40-50 / standing 50, both described as ideal for wedding ceremonies.
Katikies Hotels list 'Micro weddings' as a package idea in Santorini or Mykonos, describing small, exclusive ceremonies with Aegean views; its events and concierge team plan and manage the wedding.

Mystique Hotel (Oia, Santorini; linked to Marriott's Luxury Collection) has a 'Marry me in Santorini' Weddings page: wedding specialists organise the wedding, the couple can get ready with the bridal party in a sea-view suite, and Elios Spa offers pre-wedding treatments. Ceremony capacity, ceremony types and exclusive use are not published on the page. Venue type: caldera hotel.

As at November 2026, Smartraveller's 'Getting married overseas' page (last updated 18/08/2026, read live 11 November 2026, unchanged from paros-wedding-venues fact_302) says some countries ask you to prove you are free to marry, most commonly with a Certificate of No Impediment to Marriage (CNI) and certificates from a registry of births, deaths and marriages (a statement of no record of a previous marriage, a Single Status certificate or a No Record Result certificate); local authorities may also ask for divorce papers, a deceased spouse's death certificate, and your original birth certificate and passport. DFAT can issue a CNI in Australia, but some local authorities only accept CNIs issued in their country, so ask the destination's embassy or consulate whether you need a CNI, whether you can get it in Australia, and whether it also needs an authentication or apostille. It says each country decides what proof it accepts and there may be different regional and national laws. The Wedded Advisor confirms current requirements.

As at November 2026, Smartraveller (read live 11 November 2026, unchanged from paros-wedding-venues fact_303) says you cannot register an overseas marriage in Australia, but in most cases it is legally recognised if, when it took place, it was valid under the law of the country where it happened and would have been valid under Australian law had it occurred in Australia. A foreign marriage certificate is usually accepted as proof of the marriage but may not work as proof of a name change (check with your local registry of births, deaths and marriages), and Smartraveller suggests talking to a lawyer to confirm the certificate is valid in Australia. The Wedded Advisor confirms current requirements.

As at November 2026, Smartraveller (read live 11 November 2026) says Australia does not recognise overseas marriages where one or both people are already married to someone else, not old enough to marry, too closely related, or forced to marry.

As at November 2026, the Australian Embassy in Athens (read live 11 November 2026, unchanged from paros-wedding-venues fact_304) lists among its notarial services witnessing application forms for, and issuing, Certificates of No Impediment (CNI), witnessing notices of intended marriage, and legalisation of signatures and/or seals by authentication or apostille. An appointment is needed for all notarial services (Monday to Friday, 9:00am to 12:30pm), though apostille and CNI documents can be submitted by post; apostilled documents and CNIs are available for collection within two working days unless same-day collection is arranged in advance, or can be returned by mail. The Embassy gives no legal advice, does not witness signatures on overseas documents, honorary consuls cannot provide notarial services, and a fee applies (amounts not recorded). The Wedded Advisor confirms current requirements.

As at November 2026, Smartraveller's overall advice level for Greece is 'Exercise normal safety precautions' (page updated 30 September 2026, shown as still current when read live 11 November 2026 UTC). It notes Greece is in an active seismic zone with earthquakes and volcanic activity, including near Santorini, and that wildfires occur in the extended summer period, June to September.

As at November 2026, Smartraveller's Greece advice says same-sex relationships are legal, though attitudes vary; it advises avoiding public displays of affection, especially in rural areas, and says attitudes are generally more accepting on islands such as Mykonos, Santorini and Ios. The page does not address same-sex civil marriage.

As at November 2026, Smartraveller's Greece advice says Greece is in the Schengen area; Australians can make short trips without a visa for up to 90 days in any 180-day period, and on arrival for a short stay on an Australian passport you register fingerprints and a photo under the European Entry/Exit System (EES), which is free and needs no action before arrival, though it may cause delays at borders. Depending on why you are travelling and how long you stay you may need a visa, and entry conditions can change at short notice, so contact the nearest Greek embassy or consulate. The Wedded Advisor confirms current requirements.

Visit Greece (the official Greek tourism site) says Santorini, known in ancient times as Thera, is at the southernmost point of the Cyclades and comprises a complex of islands: Thera, Thirasia, Aspronisi, Palea Kameni and Nea Kameni. It says the island owes its fame to its active volcano, in whose caldera you can stay, and that hamlets spread across the rim of the caldera.

Visit Greece describes Santorini's beaches as black, red and white sand, multicoloured pebbles and steep cliffs, and says the island is arid with fertile soil, mainly growing vines, yellow split peas and tomatoes. The page names no individual villages (Oia, Fira, Imerovigli and Pyrgos are not named on the page as read).

Visit Greece lists flights from Athens International Airport (Eleftherios Venizelos) to Santorini Airport with a travel duration of 50 minutes, and from Thessaloniki Airport (Macedonia) to Santorini Airport of 1 hour and 30 minutes (scheduled durations stated by the tourism board). The page as read gives no ferry route or crossing time from Piraeus.

The official website of Santorini Airport (JTR), served through Fraport Greece's airport systems, lists airlines serving the airport including Aegean Airlines, Olympic Air and Sky Express alongside European and Gulf carriers such as British Airways, Lufthansa, Qatar Airways, Etihad Airways, Gulf Air and FlyDubai, and has Schengen and non-Schengen departure areas. It lists ways to and from the airport by public bus and by taxi, and has an Accessible Travel section for passengers with reduced mobility.

The Hellenic National Meteorological Service (HNMS/EMY) 'Climatic Data by City' page has no Santorini (Thira) station; for the South Aegean it lists only Naxos and Rodos. Naxos is the nearest listed station and any figures must be labelled as Naxos, not Santorini.

HNMS Naxos station (lon 25.369, lat 37.081, altitude 3 m; the page states 'Data Period: None') shows monthly mean temperatures of 16.1 C in April, 19.6 C in May, 23.5 C in June, 25.1 C in July, 25.0 C in August, 23.0 C in September and 19.7 C in October. Mean maximum temperatures are 18.7, 22.1, 25.9, 27.1, 27.0, 25.1 and 21.9 C for the same months.

HNMS Naxos station shows monthly mean precipitation of 17.6 mm in April, 10.6 mm in May, 2.4 mm in June, 0.9 mm in July, 1.6 mm in August, 7.7 mm in September and 38.6 mm in October, with mean precipitation days of 6.0, 3.6, 1.1, 0.4, 0.3, 1.9 and 5.5 respectively.

HNMS Naxos station shows a prevailing wind direction of north in every month, with monthly mean wind power of 11.7 in April, 10.0 in May, 10.3 in June, 13.3 in July, 13.8 in August, 13.9 in September and 14.5 in October (units not stated on the page).

As at November 2026, Smartraveller's overall advice for Greece is 'Exercise normal safety precautions' (level green); the page was updated 30 September 2026 and shows 'still current at 12 November 2026' when read on 11 November 2026 (Australian date).

As at November 2026, Smartraveller says heatwaves are frequent over the summer months (drink plenty of water, wear light clothing, stay in air conditioning or shade, follow local authorities), and that wildfires occur during the extended summer period from June to September, including near cities and tourist locations, prompting evacuations; fires can start with little warning and travel quickly. Expect travel disruptions in areas that might be affected.

As at November 2026, Smartraveller's latest update says to be careful when swimming in Greece due to boat traffic, coastal hazards, strong currents and marine life, to check conditions and to swim at patrolled beaches where possible. It says lifeguards operate at many Greek beaches from June to September, sea conditions can change quickly, and to avoid swimming close to cliffs, rock faces or boats.

As at November 2026, Smartraveller says during the May to October tourist season to be prepared for high temperatures and large crowds at popular seaports; in most cases you will carry luggage up and down stairs on ferries; ferry services can be delayed or cancelled in bad weather, mainly due to strong winds, so check the forecast and reconfirm departures. It says on some Greek islands, such as Santorini, smaller boats or tenders carry cruise ship passengers to and from shore and passengers using tenders may have difficulty with stairs.

As at November 2026, Smartraveller says Greece is in an active seismic zone and experiences earthquakes and volcanic activity, and that Saharan dust storms occur, particularly in spring, reducing air quality and visibility.

Santo Wines (the winery of the Union of Santorini Cooperatives) is in Pyrgos, Santorini; its Wine Tourism Center sits next to the winery with a volcano view and is open all year round. Venue type: winery.
Santo Wines has a dedicated Weddings page under 'Host your event' and says it 'provides a stunning backdrop for couples', describing saying 'I do' with the caldera as witness against the setting sun.
Santo Wines' homepage describes the winery terraces as having 'a stunning view over the caldera'.
Santo Wines weddings are handled by an Event Manager (contact via the Weddings page request form). Ceremony types, capacity and exclusive-use terms are not published on the Weddings page.
Santo Wines also lists 'Events & Receptions' and 'Conferences' under Host your event, and runs a restaurant (food and wine service) and wine tasting at the Wine Tourism Center.

Venetsanos Winery (Santorini) has a 'Wedding & Events' page stating the winery 'has also been transformed in order to host the most exclusive events and weddings on the island of Santorini'. Venue type: historic winery; its homepage calls it 'the first industrial winery on the island'.

Venetsanos Winery is built on 4 levels; on the second level the Upper Terrace is an open-air area of 250 m2 overlooking the caldera, which can host the ceremony, reception, private dinner, gala and other events.

Venetsanos Winery Upper Terrace published maximum capacity: approximately 100 seated at round tables, 160 standing reception, or 100 theatre style (chairs only). Exclusive-use terms not published; costs and availability on request by email.
Venetsanos Winery offers winery tours and wine tasting with a light lunch for visitors.

Smartraveller (DFAT), 'How to get your documents legalised' (last updated 30/09/2026): ask the overseas authority which documents they need and which must be legalised; DFAT 'can't tell you what they may want'. Find out from the intended authority or legal representative whether you need an apostille or an authentication certificate.

Smartraveller: documents that are not original Australian public documents must first be notarised by an Australian Notary Public; the apostille or authentication certificate is applied directly to the document, so if you don't want originals marked, get a notarised copy legalised (and check the overseas authority accepts it).

Smartraveller: requests use the Document Legalisation Request Form, signed in front of an authorised witness, and can be lodged by appointment at an Australian Passport Office, in person at many Australian embassies, high commissions and consulates overseas (not Honorary Consul consulates), or by registered mail to the Authentications Section in Melbourne or Sydney. A fee applies (amount not recorded).

Smartraveller: processing times vary, with delays at the end of the school year and in peak holiday periods, for incomplete requests or unpaid fees, or when the issuing authority must be contacted. An Australian-issued apostille can be verified online via DFAT.

insider_details.detail: Many caldera-edge venues are sized for intimate weddings: published caldera terraces in Oia and Imerovigli seat roughly 15 to 60, so a guest list above about 60 points to a standing reception, splitting events across spaces, or a larger venue away from the cliff edge.
Use different spaces for each event of the weekend (welcome drinks, ceremony, farewell) so nothing repeats; Grace Hotel and Katikies both publish several event spaces across one or more properties.

Some cliff-top hotels require an outside wedding planner on board months ahead (Grace Hotel states a planner is required for all weddings, from at least 3 months out), so engage a planner before locking the venue date.
Ask about room blocks and buyouts early: some hotels quote blocks or a full buyout on request without a minimum room commitment, while others offer a hotel takeover as an event type.

Confirm which ceremony types a venue can host; some caldera hotels list civil, religious, symbolic and vow renewal options in their enquiry forms, which ties back to the legal-or-symbolic decision in step 1.

Treat the CNI as a first-week task rather than a final-month one: Smartraveller says some authorities only accept CNIs issued in their own country, and the Embassy in Athens needs an appointment or a postal submission with about two working days before collection, so ask the Greek side early which version they accept.

Order certified registry certificates (single status or no record) and keep original birth certificates and passports together, because Smartraveller lists these alongside divorce papers or a death certificate as documents local authorities may ask for.

A legal wedding in Greece is generally recognised at home if it was valid there and would have been valid in Australia, but the certificate may not be enough to change a name, so couples planning a name change should check with their state registry before they fly.

Couples choosing a symbolic ceremony in Santorini can marry legally in Australia first; a Greek certificate cannot be registered in Australia, it is simply recognised, which is one reason some couples prefer to sign the paperwork at home. Phrase as advice, not fact.
Count wedding week inside the Schengen 90 days in any 180-day limit when couples combine Santorini with a longer European trip.

Naxos, the nearest official HNMS station, averages under one rain day a month from June to August (0.4 in July, 0.3 in August) but 5.5 in October and 6.0 in April, so shoulder-season dates need a covered or indoor backup in writing.
Smartraveller flags frequent summer heatwaves and June to September wildfires; plan shade, water and a later ceremony time for peak-summer dates, and have a plan if roads or flights are disrupted.

Ferries can be delayed or cancelled mainly due to strong winds and guests usually carry luggage on stairs; guests coming by sea should arrive a day early, and the 50-minute flight from Athens is the simpler option for older guests.

Santorini Airport has an Accessible Travel service for passengers with reduced mobility; ask guests with mobility needs to pre-book it with their airline, and ask each venue about steps between arrival point, ceremony and reception.
Swimming close to cliffs, rocks or boats is advised against and lifeguards operate only June to September at many beaches; worth a line in the guest welcome pack for recovery-day beach plans.

For an estate setting away from the cliff-top hotels, Pyrgos and the Venetsanos terrace both look over the caldera, so a winery can still give a caldera backdrop, and the Venetsanos terrace publishes a larger capacity (160 standing) than the caldera hotel spaces already sourced (up to 60 standing at Grace, up to 40 at Canaves).
Venetsanos publishes one main open-air space for ceremony and reception, so ask in writing where the ceremony moves if wind or weather rules out the terrace.
Santo Wines publishes no capacity or ceremony details, so put guest numbers, ceremony type, exclusive use and timing on the first enquiry to its Event Manager.

Start apostilles early: the Greek authority decides which documents need legalising, originals get marked, and DFAT warns of delays in peak holiday periods, so lodge well before the Australian December and January holidays if the wedding is in the northern summer.
